title: ChangeEmailOutcome
description: The outcome of beginning an email change on the caller's own account, derived from identity_application::accounts::ChangeEmailOutcome. The response carries the challenge the verification code was delivered under and a backoff — and NO confirmation that the address was added, because it has not been. The address is added when the code is redeemed, which is a different call that this contract does not yet have.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; ChangeEmailCommand has no body and no route serves it

challenge_id.description: The challenge the verification code was delivered under. A correct code presented against the WRONG challenge must be refused, so this is what a redemption names alongside the code — it is not a decoration.

retry_after_seconds.description: How long to wait before offering a resend. A count of SECONDS, never a duration: a duration is ambiguous across the clock the server and the clock the browser think it is.

x-what-this-response-does-not-say: it does not say the address was added — it was not, and the change is unverified until a code is redeemed
it does not say the address was already on the account — that is a refusal, and refusals arrive as errors
it does not say the delivery reached anyone — a send that logs and returns success is a finding under SECURITY.md, and Phase 2's exit condition requires real delivery

x-phase.phase: Phase 5 — Applications, grants, and the self-service surface
x-phase.note: the command itself is a Phase 1/Phase 2 concern (sessions must exist before an account can be changed), and the surface that renders it is Phase 5. This contract names 5 because that is the phase the self-service surface lands in; see docs/roadmap/phases.md.
